key_insight: Current large language models can sound plausible about Colombian law while still being frequently incorrect, so legal usefulness depends on expert supervision rather than fluency.
engineering_relevance: For legal AI systems, benchmarked reliability—not just chat quality—should drive model selection, evaluation, and deployment, especially in non-U.S. jurisdictions.
method: Built an expert-validated benchmark of 1,042 Colombian law items across 10 legal areas.
Used three question formats: closed multiple-choice, semi-open, and open-ended IRAC prompts.
Evaluated 15 proprietary and open-weight models with format-specific metrics plus human and LLM-judge scoring.
evidence_signal: Closed-question accuracy ranged from 0.905 to 0.577, but free-text factual correctness stayed below 0.45 for all models, with answer relevancy negatively correlated with correctness (Spearman rho = -0.46).
watch_item: Multiple-choice scores can overstate real-world legal reliability, so deployment should require grounded sourcing and expert review rather than relying on benchmark rankings alone.
paper_title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
